incidents.vector: A threat actor breached the Northflank cloud platform; the method of initial access is still under investigation.
incidents.impact: AI-related API keys were stolen from customer accounts; Northflank disclosed the breach and urged users to rotate any AI-related keys stored on its platform.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised Ukraine's official Air Alarm application to push false alert content across the capital.
incidents.impact: The app displayed fake chemical, nuclear and street-fighting alerts for Kyiv in Russian; no air raid sirens sounded, and officials canceled the alert within 15 minutes and urged residents to remain calm.

incidents.vector: A threat actor used AI agentic tools to gain unauthorized access to Chainalysis's internal network last month.
incidents.impact: An investigation found no evidence that the attacker accessed investigation data or customer details; the company says the incident is unrelated to the Binance hack.

incidents.vector: A database belonging to the civic-engagement platform was left publicly accessible online without password protection.
incidents.impact: 42 million records were exposed to the open internet.

incidents.vector: Hackers used AI tooling to read sensitive data directly from one of the UK domain registrar's APIs.
incidents.impact: Scraped customer contact information, product information and VAT numbers were stolen in a breach that occurred in September and was disclosed this week.

incidents.vector: An Accenture employee connected an AI coding agent to a secure Pentagon system; the agent subsequently uploaded sensitive files to a third-party website.
incidents.impact: The agent ran undetected on the Pentagon network for two months; the exfiltrated files contained controlled unclassified information (CUI) and login credentials.

incidents.attacker: Belarusian and Ukrainian hacktivist groups (CyberPartisans, SilentCrow)
incidents.vector: Hacktivist groups claim to have breached Rosstat's networks roughly six months ago and disclosed the intrusion this week.
incidents.impact: The groups claim to have stolen 23TB of data, including alleged state secrets, and to have wiped databases and internal systems.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Ivanti Connect Secure VPN appliances
incidents.vector: Three chained zero-days — an authentication bypass, a missing-authentication flaw enabling root escalation (CVE-2026-111357), and a predictable file-upload path flaw (CVE-2026-118527) — combine for unauthenticated root code execution.
incidents.impact: Volexity documented in-the-wild exploitation of the full chain; Ivanti is urging all customers to update to 25.1.1.3 or 22.8R2.6, even those who already applied the October 13 patch.

incidents.victim: Foreign ministries, defense/intelligence agencies, and 19 U.S. pharmaceutical, semiconductor, defense, nuclear and financial firms, plus telecom providers in the U.S., Belgium and the Philippines
incidents.vector: An autonomous, multi-agent AI penetration-testing framework (ARTEX, paired with DeepSeek) was used to execute up to 1,500 commands per hour and pursue multiple attack paths concurrently against more than 200 targeted organizations.
incidents.impact: About 140 of 200+ targeted organizations across 14 countries were compromised or showed evidence of moderate-confidence intrusion within an 11-day span; the campaign remains active.

incidents.vector: Attackers believed to have gained access via a compromised Binance employee laptop, enabling large-scale unauthorized withdrawals from the exchange.
incidents.impact: Roughly $6.34 billion was stolen in about 20 minutes — the largest crypto theft in history; the FBI has linked the heist to the North Korean group TraderTraitor. Binance froze almost half the funds, but the remainder is unreachable, and the exchange posted $3.6 billion in net outflows after restoring withdrawals.

incidents.vector: A threat actor compromised one of Polymarket's content delivery network (CDN) providers and injected a malicious script into the website.
incidents.impact: The script drained funds from logged-in users, stealing more than $2.65 million from roughly 700 accounts; Polymarket reimbursed all affected users who reported losses.

incidents.victim: 24 Palo Alto Networks firewalls, including two U.S. government-affiliated servers
incidents.vector: An attacker used a Chinese internet-asset search engine to identify roughly 19,000 exposed firewalls, narrowed the list, then chained the PHP2Shell exploit (CVE-2026-109618/109619) with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw (CVE-2026-46300) to gain root access to PAN-OS management interfaces.
incidents.impact: 24 firewalls were compromised; on two U.S. government-affiliated servers the attacker obtained Active Directory credentials and network topology and likely retained persistent access. Palo Alto Networks has released a fixed PAN-OS management web server version.

incidents.vector: A tampered copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension (versions 2.1.312/2.1.313) was published to the Cursor Extension Marketplace — not Anthropic's or Microsoft's official channels — and silently installed an attacker SSH key and reverse SSH tunnel on load.
incidents.impact: The malicious package was live for about 11 hours on October 29 and planted SSH backdoors on an estimated 5,000 systems; Cursor removed the extension, shut down the marketplace for cleanup, and worked with a cloud provider to take down the attacker's command-and-control server.

incidents.victim: Organizations worldwide running unpatched PHP (WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and other CMS platforms)
incidents.vector: Two critical memory-corruption flaws in PHP's request-handling internals (dubbed "PHP2Shell," CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) allow unauthenticated remote code execution via a single crafted HTTP request.
incidents.impact: CISA added both CVEs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; GreyNoise confirmed at least six successful exploitations, and of roughly 42 million internet-facing PHP services, more than 10 million remained unpatched a week after disclosure.

incidents.victim: U.S. and allied businesses employing DPRK IT workers under false identities
incidents.vector: North Korean IT workers use fraudulent documents, stolen identities and AI-generated personas to secure remote employment at Western companies, then exploit their network access.
incidents.impact: Treasury's OFAC sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity based in Russia and North Korea for facilitating cryptocurrency and fiat money-laundering networks that funneled worker wages and stolen data proceeds to fund DPRK's weapons programs; IT workers have also deployed malware and exfiltrated proprietary data from employer networks.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached a financial-aid application website operated by the department.
incidents.impact: Personal data belonging to 4.9 million students was stolen; the department says financial aid itself is not at risk.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to payment processing systems, per the company's SEC filing.
incidents.impact: Payment card details belonging to customers were stolen during the breach.

incidents.victim: A water utility, telecommunications provider, regional government body and university across Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries in Europe, Africa and Latin America
incidents.vector: Exploited unpatched SharePoint ToolShell vulnerabilities for initial access, then deployed a tool that disabled security software on roughly 40 hosts within two hours before spreading Warlock ransomware via domain-wide SYSVOL replication.
incidents.impact: Warlock ransomware encrypted roughly 33 of 40 compromised hosts almost as soon as endpoint protection was disabled, disrupting operations at four organizations outside the United States over a two-month campaign.

incidents.victim: Hospitals, government entities, law firms and other businesses worldwide (Hive and Nefilim ransomware victims)
incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-service affiliate activity — the defendant gained access to victim networks and deployed Hive or Nefilim ransomware to encrypt data and extort ransom payments.
incidents.impact: Hive conspirators attacked roughly 1,500 victims worldwide from 2021-2023, causing more than $100 million in losses and disrupting hospital patient care during the COVID-19 pandemic. Affiliate Artem Stryzhak was sentenced to 70 months in prison; co-conspirator Volodymyr Tymoshchuk remains a fugitive with an $11 million reward offered for his capture.

incidents.victim: Six U.S. and Canadian law firms
incidents.vector: Suspected callback-phishing and social-engineering intrusion technique associated with a data-extortion gang that has specifically targeted U.S. law firms for the past two years.
incidents.impact: Six law firms — four in Canada and two in the U.S. — disclosed security breaches within the past week.

incidents.victim: eMudhra Limited and downstream TLS certificate holders
incidents.vector: Eight eMudhra emSign G3 intermediate certificate authority private keys were generated with insufficient cryptographic randomness, allowing the keys to be mathematically derived from their public certificates.
incidents.impact: The compromised keys could have been used to forge trusted TLS and code-signing certificates to carry out man-in-the-middle attacks; major browser and OS vendors revoked trust in the affected intermediates and eMudhra revoked the eight certificates.

incidents.victim: Approximately 600 organizations across the Americas, Europe and Australia
incidents.vector: Gains access via compromised credentials and exploitation of known vulnerabilities in internet-facing VPN devices, then uses legitimate IT tools to move laterally, disables backups, and steals data before encrypting systems.
incidents.impact: CISA, the FBI, U.S. Secret Service and international partners issued a joint advisory on SafePay, among the most active ransomware groups of 2026, with indicators of compromise and mitigation guidance.

incidents.victim: ConnectWise Cloud Backup customers (hundreds of Microsoft 365 tenants)
incidents.vector: A threat actor obtained a highly sensitive API secret that allowed ConnectWise Cloud Backup to connect to customers' Microsoft 365 environments, enabling unauthorized sign-ins without triggering multi-factor authentication.
incidents.impact: Huntress observed sign-in activity across nearly 1,000 Entra tenants with more than 300 successful sign-ins and confirmed unauthorized access in 162 tenants; ConnectWise suspended its Cloud Backup, SaaS Security and Cloud Management services during remediation.

incidents.victim: U.S.-based tax preparation businesses and their customers
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — tax fraud and identity theft
incidents.vector: Spearphishing emails were used to gain access to tax preparation firms' systems, then used to steal clients' personal and tax identifying information.
incidents.impact: Conspirators hacked several U.S. tax businesses in New York, Texas and other states, stealing data on roughly 800 customers to file fraudulent tax returns and disaster-loan claims, obtaining more than $3.3 million in fraudulent proceeds; defendant Chukwuemeka Victor Amachukwu was sentenced to eight years in prison.

incidents.vector: An unidentified third party misused the company's member information retrieval API.
incidents.impact: 22,519,960 customer records were compromised, including names, email addresses, passwords, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth and employment information.
